question.problem: Write $\frac{4x-1}{4x-7}$ in the form $a+\frac{b}{4x-7},$ where $a\ne 0.$ What is the value of $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we subtract and add $7$ in the numerator. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x-1}{4x-7}=\frac{4x-7+7-1}{4x-7}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x-7+7-1}{4x-7} & =\frac{4x-7}{4x-7}+\frac{7-1}{4x-7} \\  & =1+\frac{6}{4x-7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have $a=1$ and $b=6,$ and we get

$$
a+b=1+6=7.
$$
